description: Deterministic 90-day cash flow forecasting engine that synthesizes recurring cashflows (Feature 19), Plaid liability obligations, seasonal discretionary spending patterns, and manually planned one-time expenses into a day-by-day balance projection with confidence bands, danger zone detection, and scenario toggling. Turns Family Pulse from a rearview mirror into a windshield.

timing.gatingCondition: Feature 19 (Recurring Cashflow Intelligence) must be shipped and running. The recurring_expenses table provides the structured recurring income and expense schedules that make the forecast meaningful. Without it, the engine would have to guess at recurring charges.

principles: Deterministic math, not LLM — the forecast is a reproducible day-by-day ledger computation. LLM narrates results but never computes them. This makes forecasts testable, instant, and explainable.
Confidence bands over point estimates — a single line implies false precision. Bands communicate uncertainty honestly and widen over the forecast horizon.
Feature 19 is a hard dependency — recurring detection provides the structured recurring income and expense schedule that is the backbone of the forecast.
Liability minimum payments are forecasted from Plaid liability data only; matching recurring debt-service transactions are excluded from recurring expense inputs to prevent double-counting.
Planned expenses are simple data entry, not financial planning software — name, amount, date, done.
Forecast refreshes automatically after sync but is cached between syncs — never stale, never wastefully recomputed.
Daily granularity is sufficient — charges post daily, intra-day precision is noise.
The forecast is the foundation for deferred Feature 9 (Planning & Goals) — savings signal, goal projections, and tuition horizons all derive from forecast data.
SECRETS INVARIANT: forecast data contains only derived amounts and dates — no account numbers, tokens, or raw Plaid data in API responses or LLM context.

techStack.database: PostgreSQL — new planned_expenses and cash_flow_snapshots tables; reads from recurring_expenses, accounts, transactions
techStack.charting: Chart.js 4.x with chartjs-plugin-annotation for danger zone markers and confidence band fills
techStack.testing: node:test for forecast engine (deterministic inputs → expected outputs), seasonal baseline, danger zone detection, and API coverage

userStories.title: Seasonal spending baseline computation
acceptanceCriteria: Compute historical discretionary spending by calendar month from transactions excluding transfers, income, hidden transactions, and transactions mapped to active recurring cashflow items
Use at least 12 months of data when available (Monarch import + Plaid combined)
For months with <12 months of history, use available data with a wider confidence adjustment
Exclude the current (incomplete) month from the baseline
Use median monthly discretionary spend by calendar month for v1 to reduce outlier skew
Output: { month: 1-12, avg_total: number, avg_recurring: number, avg_discretionary: number, sample_months: number }
Handle edge case: no history for a calendar month (use overall monthly average as fallback)
userStories.testStrategy: node:test with fixture transaction data spanning 14 months. Verify per-month averages, recurring subtraction, sparse month fallback, and current month exclusion.

userStories.title: Core forecast engine — day-by-day projection
acceptanceCriteria: Takes as input: starting_balance, recurring_income (from Feature 19), recurring_expenses (from Feature 19), liability_payments (from accounts table), seasonal_baseline, planned_expenses, horizon_days (default 90)
Produces an array of { date, projected_balance, confidence_low, confidence_high, events: [] } for each day
Starting balance uses balance-policy.js sumAccountBalances for all depository accounts
Inputs are fully materialized schedules, not raw transactions
Recurring income added on detected schedule dates (e.g., biweekly paycheck pattern)
Recurring expenses subtracted on projected next-occurrence dates using expected_next_date and schedule anchors from Feature 19
Liability minimum payments subtracted on due dates from Plaid data
Discretionary daily burn = (seasonal_discretionary_avg for that calendar month) / days_in_month
Planned one-time expenses subtracted on their scheduled date
Month-end and short-month edge cases are handled explicitly for recurring monthly items
Confidence bands use a deterministic heuristic based on forecast horizon and historical discretionary volatility, or are omitted in v1 if not yet calibrated
Events array lists what happened on each day (income, charge name, planned expense, liability payment)
Engine is a pure function with no side effects — fully testable with fixture inputs
userStories.testStrategy: node:test with deterministic fixture inputs. Test: (1) simple case — one paycheck, one expense, 30 days. (2) Complex — multiple income streams, recurring at different frequencies, liability payments, seasonal adjustment, planned expense. (3) Edge: paycheck on weekend, month boundary, leap year. (4) Verify balance never goes negative without danger zone flagging. (5) Confidence band width increases monotonically.

userStories.title: Danger zone detection
acceptanceCriteria: Configurable safety floor via app_config key cash_flow_safety_floor (default $3,000)
If projected_balance drops below safety floor on any day, flag as danger zone
Danger zone output: { date, projected_balance, deficit_below_floor, trigger_event }
Multiple danger zones possible (balance recovers then drops again)
If confidence_low (pessimistic band) crosses floor but projected doesn't, flag as 'at_risk' (not 'danger')
GET /api/cash-flow/danger-zones returns all upcoming danger/at-risk dates
Dashboard integration: if any danger zone within 30 days, show alert banner
userStories.testStrategy: node:test: (1) no danger zone when balance stays healthy. (2) Danger zone triggered by large planned expense. (3) Multiple danger zones with recovery between. (4) At-risk when only pessimistic band crosses. (5) Dashboard banner logic for 30-day window.

userStories.title: Monthly surplus/deficit summary cards
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/cash-flow/monthly-outlook returns next 3 months with: { month, expected_income, expected_recurring, expected_discretionary, expected_liability_payments, planned_expenses_total, net_surplus_or_deficit, projected_end_balance }
Income from detected recurring income patterns (Feature 19)
Recurring from Feature 19 committed total for that month
Discretionary from seasonal baseline for that calendar month
Liability payments from Plaid due dates falling in that month
Planned expenses from planned_expenses table for that month
Net = income - recurring - discretionary - liability - planned
End balance = prior month end balance + net (chained from current balance)
userStories.testStrategy: node:test: verify month-over-month chaining (end balance of month 1 = start of month 2). Verify all components sum correctly. Edge: planned expense spanning month boundary assigned to correct month.

userStories.title: Planned expenses CRUD
acceptanceCriteria: New table: planned_expenses (id, name, amount, scheduled_date, status, notes, created_by, created_at, updated_at)
POST /api/cash-flow/planned-expenses — create (parent-only)
GET /api/cash-flow/planned-expenses — list all active
PATCH /api/cash-flow/planned-expenses/:id — update amount, date, status, notes (parent-only)
DELETE /api/cash-flow/planned-expenses/:id — soft delete via status='deleted' (parent-only)
Validation: amount > 0, scheduled_date in the future (or within current month), name required
Status values: active, completed, deleted
Examples: 'Alex Pacific Rim trip' ($6000, Oct 2026), 'New tires' ($800, May 2026)
userStories.testStrategy: node:test: CRUD operations, validation (missing name, negative amount, past date), parent-only auth, soft delete, recurring expansion over horizon.

userStories.title: Forecast caching and refresh
acceptanceCriteria: After each Plaid sync, forecast is recomputed and cached in cash_flow_snapshots table
Cache stores: computed_at, horizon_days, starting_balance, daily_projections (JSONB), danger_zones (JSONB), monthly_outlook (JSONB)
GET /api/cash-flow/forecast returns cached forecast if its input fingerprint still matches current sync timestamp, recurring data updated_at, planned expenses updated_at, and relevant config values
If cache is stale or missing, recompute on demand and cache
Force refresh: POST /api/cash-flow/forecast/refresh (parent-only)
Cache is single-row (latest forecast), old rows cleaned up
Forecast computation targets <500ms for 90-day horizon (pure JS math, no LLM)
userStories.testStrategy: node:test: cache hit returns stored data. Cache miss triggers recomputation. Force refresh replaces cache. Stale detection based on sync timestamp.

userStories.title: Cash flow forecast page (frontend)

Chart x-axis: dates. Chart y-axis: dollar amounts. Tooltip shows date, projected balance, events

userStories.title: Dashboard forecast widget
acceptanceCriteria: Dashboard gains a forecast summary section below the existing coverage indicator
Shows: 90-day outlook status badge (healthy/caution/danger), next danger zone if any, next month projected surplus/deficit
Clicking the widget navigates to forecast.html
If no forecast data exists yet (Feature 19 hasn't run), shows a muted 'Forecast available after first sync' placeholder
Does not add more than 3 lines to the dashboard — information density matters
userStories.testStrategy: node:test: forecast summary API returns correct status badge logic. Playwright: widget renders on dashboard with link to forecast page.

userStories.title: LLM context enrichment with forecast data
acceptanceCriteria: context-assembler adds forecast summary to weekly, monthly, and query contexts
Context includes: 90_day_outlook_status, next_danger_zone (date + deficit), monthly_outlook (next 3 months surplus/deficit), planned_expenses_total, current_liquid_balance, projected_90_day_balance
Weekly digest can now say: 'Looking ahead: April projects a $340 deficit due to car insurance renewal. Current trajectory keeps you above your $3,000 safety floor through June.'
What-if scenarios gain structured forecast baseline: instead of LLM guessing, the what-if prompt includes actual forecast numbers as the starting point
All forecast context passes through sanitizeForLLM
userStories.testStrategy: node:test: verify forecast context structure, verify sanitization, verify graceful empty state when no forecast exists.

userStories.title: What-If enhancement with forecast overlay
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/magic/what-if gains an optional forecast_overlay response field

When a what-if scenario is submitted, the engine: (1) computes baseline forecast, (2) parses the scenario into a planned expense equivalent, (3) computes modified forecast, (4) returns both baseline and modified trajectories
The LLM prompt now includes structured forecast comparison data, not just a text snapshot
Reports page What-If section can optionally show a mini chart comparing baseline vs scenario trajectory
Fallback: if scenario can't be parsed into a planned expense (too abstract), falls back to current LLM-only approach
userStories.testStrategy: node:test: parseable scenario produces forecast overlay with baseline and modified trajectories. Unparseable scenario falls back gracefully. Manual: verify mini chart renders on reports page.

high: Forecast accuracy depends entirely on Feature 19's recurring detection quality. If recurring income (paychecks) or major expenses are missed, the forecast will be misleading. Mitigation: the forecast page should show what assumptions it's making (detected income, detected recurring charges) so Eric can spot-check. Add a 'forecast assumptions' expandable section.
medium: Seasonal baseline may be skewed by one-time large expenses in historical data (e.g., a $5,000 medical bill in March 2025 inflates March's average). Mitigation: use median rather than mean for seasonal baseline, and cap discretionary at 2× the 12-month overall average to limit outlier impact.

Confidence bands are heuristic, not statistically derived. Mitigation: clearly label them as 'estimated range' not 'confidence interval'. Calibrate the scaling factor after observing real forecast-vs-actual divergence over 2-3 months.

Planned expenses are manual data entry — Eric has to remember to add them. Mitigation: the forecast page should prompt 'Any upcoming large expenses?' and the LLM digest can remind him when the planned expenses list is empty.
low: Chart.js annotation plugin needed for danger zone markers and confidence bands. Mitigation: chartjs-plugin-annotation is a well-maintained CDN-loadable plugin, same loading pattern as Chart.js itself.
Forecast computation time for 90-day horizon. Mitigation: pure JS math with no DB queries during computation (all inputs pre-fetched). Target <500ms is easily achievable.

Nav bar now has 7 entries (Dashboard, Accounts, Transactions, Budget, Recurring, Forecast, Reports). Mitigation: this is the natural grouping — past (Transactions) → present (Budget) → recurring (Recurring) → future (Forecast). Reports is the analytical summary. Settings remains in its own section.
